_metadata.data_period: 2024-2026 (Appcast 2024/2025 funnel data, WordStream Apr 2025-Mar 2026 Google, WordStream 2025 Facebook, SHRM 2025, Indeed 2026 current pricing)
_metadata.vintage_note: Refreshed 2026-06-13 to incorporate named industry sources (Appcast 2025 & 2026 Recruitment Marketing Benchmark Reports, SHRM 2025 Benchmarking, WordStream/LocaliQ 2026 Google & 2025 Facebook, Indeed official pricing). Google Ads recruitment CPC/CPA and Meta recruitment values were refreshed from WordStream named-source figures (prior values were from secondary marketing blogs and are retained as prior_value where superseded). LinkedIn, programmatic, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor and TikTok figures sourced only to third-party aggregators are tagged confidence:low with their named source. 2026-06-13 also ADDED four previously-missing platforms (reddit_ads, snapchat_ads, youtube_ads, pinterest_ads). IMPORTANT: no recruitment-specific named benchmark exists for any of these four - every figure is a GENERAL-market / B2B aggregator benchmark (Benly, AdBacklog, AdLiftr, Store Growers, WebFX), so all are tagged confidence:low and explicitly noted as not recruitment-specific. Reddit B2B/Tech is the closest recruitment proxy; Pinterest is a weak-fit channel for recruitment.

appcast_funnel._note: Industry-wide US recruitment-media funnel benchmarks from Appcast's annual Recruitment Marketing Benchmark Reports. These are the authoritative cross-channel apply-rate / CPC / CPA / CPH figures.
appcast_funnel.cost_per_hire_note_2024: Flat through most of 2024, slight year-end increase
appcast_funnel.directional_trend_2025: Cost-per-application (CPA) and cost-per-hire (CPH) rose sharply in 2025 despite a softer labor market (driven by job-board pricing shifts and programmatic media models); apply rates remained high. Specific dollar medians are gated in the paid report.

indeed_sponsored._avg_cpc_range_usd_refreshed_2026_07_25: Refreshed from the retired earlier-vintage band to 0.97-2.71, the cited July-2026 typical US-role band in channel_benchmarks_seed.json (336480d; Pin.com citing ThePricer 2026/ShiftNow 2025/Job Board Doctor May 2025, aggregator-inferred). third_party_estimates.cpc_range_usd 0.10-5.00 matches that research's full observed spread and is unchanged. channel_comparison_recruitment's Indeed Sponsored point value was moved onto the same basis in the same commit. reddit_ads.model_note: General-market 2026 pricing. NO recruitment-specific named benchmark exists; closest proxy is the B2B/Tech vertical, which is the best fit for recruitment targeting tech/professional candidates via interest and subreddit targeting.

b2b_tech_vertical_usd.note: B2B/Tech is the proxy vertical for recruitment; no Jobs/Employment/Staffing row exists in any named Reddit benchmark source

reddit_ads.best_for: Reaching engaged niche/professional communities (tech, trades, gaming, finance) via subreddit targeting; employer branding and passive-candidate awareness. Cheap for attention (CPC/CPM) but conversion depends heavily on message match and low friction.

sources.metric: Median CPC $1.25 (range $0.50-$3.00; broad ~$0.75, subreddit ~$1.20); CPM range $3-$12 (broad ~$4.50, interest ~$6.00, subreddit ~$8.00); B2B/Tech CPC $1.80-$2.50; high-value B2B CPM ~$12.00; B2B CPL SaaS $50-$120, Dev Tools $40-$100 - GENERAL, not recruitment-specific
sources.source: Benly 'Reddit Ads Cost: CPC, CPM & CPA by Industry (2026)' (third-party compilation; general-market, not recruitment-specific)

sources.metric: All-industries 2026 ranges: CTR 0.2%-1.2%; CPC $0.10-$2.50; CPM $1-$12; CVR <2%-15%; CPA $2-$150+. No Jobs/Employment/Staffing industry row exists; B2B SaaS commands highest CPC ($0.60-$2.50) - GENERAL, not recruitment-specific
sources.source: AdBacklog 'Reddit Ads Benchmarks Per Industry (2026)' (third-party aggregator; no recruitment row)

snapchat_ads.model_note: General-market 2026 pricing (DTC/ecommerce-skewed dataset). NO recruitment-specific named benchmark exists. Strong fit for early-career and hourly hiring and employer branding to Gen-Z/younger audiences via vertical video.
snapchat_ads.best_for: Early-career, hourly and high-volume hiring; employer branding to Gen-Z and younger candidates through native vertical video (Stories, Spotlight). Cheapest social CPC at scale; lead-gen CPM is high so favor traffic/awareness objectives for recruitment.

sources.metric: Median CPC $0.84 (IQR $0.51-$1.34; Traffic $0.71, Conversions $1.18); median CPM by objective Awareness $5.84 / Engagement $9.10 / Traffic $11.20 / Lead Gen $24.80 / Conversions $27.10; median DTC first-purchase CPA $23.40; B2B SaaS lead-gen CPA $58.40; CTR 1.04% - GENERAL (2,431 campaigns / 412 advertisers Feb-May 2026, DTC-skewed), not recruitment-specific
sources.source: AdLiftr 'Snapchat Ads Cost 2026: CPM, CPC, CPA Benchmarks' (third-party compilation; general-market)

youtube_ads.model_note: General-market 2026 pricing (Google Ads video network). NO recruitment-specific named benchmark exists. Best used for recruitment-marketing reach, employer branding and awareness rather than direct apply-driving.
youtube_ads.best_for: Employer-branding and recruitment-marketing reach/awareness (skippable in-stream and Shorts); top-of-funnel candidate attraction and retargeting to careers-site visitors. Low CPV makes it efficient for views, but weak as a direct apply/conversion channel.

sources.metric: CPV ~$0.05 in-stream (Shorts $0.10-$0.30); CPM $5-$10 (market avg ~$9.29; CTV $8.72-$10.01); CPC ~$3.56 ($0.05-$10.71); view rate 31.9%; CTR 0.65% - GENERAL industry benchmarks, not recruitment-specific
sources.source: Store Growers 'YouTube Ads Benchmarks (2026)' (named third-party; general-market)

pinterest_ads.model_note: General-market 2026 pricing (WebFX survey of 270 marketers; no industry segmentation). NO recruitment-specific named benchmark exists - Pinterest has no Jobs/Employment row in any named source and is a weak-fit, niche recruitment channel.

avg_cpm_range_usd.note: WebFX survey: majority $0.00-$1.50; higher tier >$7.00 used by ~10% of advertisers

pinterest_ads.best_for: Niche / weak fit for recruitment. Possible use only for highly visual, female-skewing or lifestyle-adjacent employer branding (e.g. beauty, retail, hospitality, creative roles). Not a primary apply-driving channel; figures are general DTC/consumer benchmarks.

sources.metric: CPC $0.10-$1.50 (most $0.00-$0.20; competitive $0.70-$1.50); CPM ~$2-$5 (majority $0.00-$1.50, >$7 high tier); CPA $2-$8 - GENERAL (WebFX survey of 270 marketers, no industry segmentation), not recruitment-specific
